title: One ticket on bus then tram

turns.user: I have one ordinary BKK single ticket. I'll ride a bus for 10 minutes.
turns.agent:
For one ordinary 10-minute bus ride, your single ticket should be suitable, assuming the bus is within the ticket’s applicable area and you make no voluntary transfer to another street-level service. Validate it as required for the ticket medium before or when starting the ride; the snapshot doesn’t specify the exact validation steps for your ticket type.

An ordinary single ticket is generally for one continuous one-way ride on a bus, tram, trolleybus, or suburban service; a voluntary transfer between street-level services normally needs another ticket. It is not valid on 100E. BKK: Single ticket (fare snapshot dated 5 November 2026).

Is this an ordinary bus, rather than 100E, and is your ticket paper or mobile?

turns.user: Then I want to board a tram to finish the trip. Can I reuse that same single ticket?
turns.agent:
Usually, no. If you get off the bus and board a tram, that’s a voluntary transfer between street-level services, so you’ll normally need a second ordinary single ticket for the tram. The exception described in the snapshot is changing between metro lines in the same direction—not a bus-to-tram transfer.

This is based on the fare snapshot dated 5 November 2026; check BKK’s single-ticket rules for current details. If you stay on the same bus for the whole ride, the ordinary single is generally for that continuous one-way trip.
